messages:
FinEdge (customer): hitting intermittent SSE disconnects from /v1/stream since yesterday afternoon. clients see partial output (last chunk), then connection closed. Happening across multiple regions but more pronounced for EU users. Logs show `write EPIPE` on our side. Any known degradations?

Maya (support): sorry you're seeing this — we'll dig in. do you have a repro and any request/response logs you can paste? also, are you using our hosted API or Dedicated/Private?

FinEdge (customer): hosted API. repro is simple: Node EventSource and curl -N both fail after ~20-40s when client is artificially slow. here's our minimal repro:

```
# client side (node)
const EventSource = require('eventsource');
const es = new EventSource('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=small');
es.onmessage = (e) => { console.log('event', e.data); setTimeout(()=>{}, 5000); } // intentionally block the main loop to simulate slow consumer
```

# or from shell
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=small" | pv -qL 50
```

FinEdge (customer): server logs from our side (we're behind Envoy/proxy):

```
[2026-02-25T14:20:56Z] INFO conn=abc123 path=/v1/stream event=started
[2026-02-25T14:21:20Z] WARN conn=abc123 outstanding_bytes=90512 write_blocked=true
[2026-02-25T14:21:26Z] ERROR conn=abc123 write EPIPE, syscall=write
[2026-02-25T14:21:26Z] INFO conn=abc123 closed reason=client_slow_consumer
```

FinEdge (customer): we see partial event stream in the client (last event truncated). how does Redwood handle slow consumers/backpressure?

Maya (support): thanks — that log points to server-side writes failing due to backpressure. tagging Theo from runtime. @Theo can you weigh in on typical behaviors?

Theo (eng-runtime): yup, this is classic slow-consumer/backpressure. quick summary: when the consumer stops reading fast enough, the TCP send buffer grows and eventually writes return EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK or EPIPE (if peer closed). Our streaming runtime has per-connection outstanding_bytes limit (default 64k) and a hard disconnect if the consumer is stalled past threshold (default 30s) to protect capacity.

Theo (eng-runtime): couple of things to check:
- are you seeing this only behind Envoy/proxy or direct to our API?
- can you reproduce without the proxy (direct curl to api.redwood.ai) to rule out Envoy buffering/timeouts?

FinEdge (customer): repro is with Envoy in front. we can try direct but we prefer using the proxy for production.

Priya (oncall): ENV NOTE: Envoy defaults can buffer downstream responses. if proxy buffers are large and downstream stops reading, you'll still hit write backpressure at the proxy -> upstream socket. check `proxy_buffer_size` / `stream_idle_timeout`. Also Envoy may send a 503 or reset if idle timeouts hit.

envoy-bot: suggested config to enable true streaming:
```
# envoy config snippet
http_connection_manager:
  use_remote_address: true
  stream_idle_timeout: 0s # avoid idle timeouts closing streaming connections
  xff_num_trusted_hops: 1
  codec_type: AUTO
```

Maya (support): for Hosted API we sometimes enforce hard limits to avoid noisy neighbors. Past cases were resolved by either (a) reducing per-event size so clients can consume partials and keep reading, (b) decreasing server flush interval (send smaller chunks more frequently), or (c) increasing per-connection outstanding_bytes for long-polling customers if SLA allows.

FinEdge (customer): curious — what's the recommended approach? our events can be several KB each (embedding + metadata).

Theo (eng-runtime): recommended immediate mitigations:
1) Change client to read in a streaming-friendly manner (don't block main loop; use small buffer reads). For Node, avoid CPU blocking in onmessage handlers.
2) Emit smaller events: break up large model outputs into multiple `data:` events of ~1-4KB.
3) If you're stuck behind Envoy, set `stream_idle_timeout: 0s` and disable buffering at proxy layer.
4) We can increase the outstanding_bytes limit for your tenant as a short-term mitigation but that raises risk of resource tie-up.

Theo (eng-runtime): also on our side we can: honor `Connection: keep-alive` and use `socket.setNoDelay(true)` to reduce latency, and ensure we check the `drain` event in Node/C++ runtime so we don't block the runtime thread. Our runtime currently closes after N seconds of stopped progress to protect throughput.

FinEdge (customer): can you give us steps to repro from your side? we'd like a joint test.

Maya (support): yes. we'll repro with a slow-reader harness and share results. quick repro plan:
1) start a streaming call with curl -N and pipe through `pv -qL 40` to throttle read speed
2) watch for `write EPIPE` on the server side and `Connection reset by peer` on client
3) try with envoy proxy config change (stream_idle_timeout=0s + disable buffering)
4) try breaking events to 1KB chunks

Theo (eng-runtime): here's a minimal server-side repro we used locally (node) to simulate blocked downstream backpressure:
```
const http = require('http');
http.createServer((req, res) => {
  res.writeHead(200, {
    'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream',
    'Cache-Control': 'no-cache',
    'Connection': 'keep-alive'
  });

  // write large event every 1s
  let i = 0;
  const id = setInterval(() => {
    const payload = 'x'.repeat(8000); // large chunk
    const ok = res.write(`data: ${payload}\n\n`);
    if (!ok) {
      console.warn('write returned false -> backpressure, pausing writes');
      clearInterval(id);
      // listen for drain
      res.once('drain', () => { console.log('drain event, resuming'); /* resume interval */ });
    }
  }, 1000);
});
```

Priya (oncall): if customers can't change clients, we usually: (1) change server behavior to produce smaller chunks, (2) crank up outstanding byte limit temporarily, (3) add instrumentation to detect slow-consumers and surface them in Console (so SRE can correlate traffic).

FinEdge (customer): is there any billing impact? we saw higher token counts because of repeated reconnects.

Maya (support): good call — reconnect storms can increase billing by reissuing the same request. we'll open a billing review if our changes don't mitigate within the next 24h. please include timestamps of reconnects and estimated token counts.

ops-bot: opened ticket RW-3421 (priority=P2) assigned to eng-runtime: investigate SSE slow-consumer disconnects for FinEdge.

- run repro harness against their account (with permission)
- test Envoy proxy config changes to ensure streaming behavior is preserved
- evaluate increasing per-connection outstanding_bytes for FinEdge to 128k as a short term
- add a server-side metric `streaming.consumer_stalls` to be able to alert on this pattern

FinEdge (customer): thx — we'll try to change client to smaller reads and test envoy config. we'll post results here.

Maya (support): one more quick tip: when using curl, use `--no-buffer` sometimes helps, but the real fix is smaller events or faster client consumption.

FinEdge (customer): quick update — flipped envoy `stream_idle_timeout` to 0 and disabled upstream buffering, re-ran the throttled curl and survived 90s with no disconnect. looks promising.

Maya (support): excellent — marking in ticket. Priya/theo, can you follow up on server-side mitigations so we don't rely on customers changing proxy configs?

Priya (oncall): yes, I'll take RW-3421 and prototype streaming metric and a safe limit bump for this tenant.

Theo (eng-runtime): will prototype smaller-chunk behavior toggle and a runtime flag to increase outstanding_bytes per-tenant. will post PR and release notes.

Maya (support): closing loop here once FinEdge confirms production traffic stable for 48h. thanks all :heart:
